additional_concerns: The transition preserves an existing application process; it does not expressly establish blanket substantive ineligibility. Candidates node.1bf6918f69c6b37738daeb83, node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e, node.ce439b1cf9ed8301fbb68f94 and node.ea4d19630f8cab09065b1909 encode that additional inference. Preserved processing might prevent bypassing the pending application without permanently disqualifying the change; the supplied source does not resolve this distinction.

The transition facts are frozen at commencement. Subsequent approval, withdrawal or resubmission could matter to actual relief, but their effects are not supplied. No permanent exclusion should be inferred from historical pending status alone.

Candidate node.4d548f2e09bc36ef51212f64 excludes legacy applications from its question scope rather than deciding their eligibility. Candidate node.b66b3e831bb98a12db59dffa answers only substantive qualification. Their narrower answers must not be presented as comprehensive actual-relief determinations.

The stated commencement date is supported, but the source does not fully specify which assessment or implementation event controls every transitional case. Candidate node.4e6a162c35678e9ddf17ad8e should clarify whether its temporal scope concerns assessment date or proposed implementation date.

Actual home compliance and the novelty, complexity and possible local-policy classifications remain supplied judgments. Applying these predicates requires applicable home-jurisdiction rules and relevant SFC guidance, neither of which is substantively supplied.

The updated SFC FAQs and the existing approval or authorisation process are missing for resolving actual procedural relief. The two supplied dependency IDs have null source hashes and no descriptive mapping; neither can reliably be assigned to those authorities.

The introductory reference to home-regulator supervision does not clearly impose a separate item (ii) condition beyond its express home-requirements test. Preserve that interpretive distinction pending the relevant FAQs.
Removal of prior approval does not remove notification, filing or post-vetting obligations. Their exclusion from these narrowly typed questions is not a general compliance determination.
